statement: For interval scheduling (selecting a maximum number of pairwise non-overlapping intervals), repeatedly choosing the remaining interval of shortest duration and discarding everything that conflicts with it yields a maximum-size schedule.
definitions: Intervals are half-open [s,f); two intervals conflict iff they intersect; the greedy must return a strictly smaller schedule than optimum under every tie-breaking rule (e.g. use distinct durations).
ground_truth_witness: Three classes on one day, half-open intervals: L = [0,10), M = [9,11), R = [10,20). Durations are 10, 2, 10, so the shortest-duration greedy picks M first; M conflicts with both L (they overlap on [9,10)) and R (they overlap on [10,11)), so both are discarded and greedy returns 1 class. The optimum is {L, R}: L ends at 10 and R starts at 10, so they do not overlap - 2 classes.
